# CoCoFlow CI and release gates

The new Unity gate is being introduced by 0.4.7 task P003. Keep the existing
required check, `CI Static / gate`, until the complete workflow has real passing
and failing evidence and the maintainer authorizes the ruleset change to
`CI / gate`. Local script checks or successful license activation do not prove
that package tests passed.

## What runs

| Check | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `CI Static / gate` | Diff hygiene, accidentally tracked ignored files, result-reader tests, current release metadata, and change classification |
| `Unity / complete package` | A new host, complete dependencies, real Unity compilation, package EditMode and PlayMode, strict XML/suite checks, and seat cleanup |
| `CI / gate` | Always summarizes applicable jobs; failed, cancelled, missing, or required-but-skipped Unity does not pass |
| `Release / identity` | Checks tag/package/current-doc identity and successful `CI / gate` on that commit; does not rerun tests or publish |

Documentation-only PRs can skip Unity. Unknown files, source, tests, assets,
assemblies, dependencies, and execution configuration require it. A package
version-only change can skip Unity on a task PR; final PRs into master, master
pushes and manual runs always execute the complete suite. External PRs never
receive Unity credentials. Their code needs a trusted candidate with real Unity
results before release; skipped Unity is not a pass.

## Disposable host and complete dependencies

The checkout stays at the Git workspace root. Preparation copies the current
package into `.ci-work/package` and creates `.ci-work/host` beside it.
The manifest references `file:../../package` and marks CoCoFlow testable.
No business scenes, Graphs, previous Library, or stale XML are carried over.

| Input | CI configuration |
| --- | --- |
| Runner / Editor | Windows Server 2022 / native Unity `6000.3.27f2` |
| GameCI | Official CLI `v0.1.72` Windows executable, checked by SHA-256; native HostRunner |
| Product dependencies | UPM resolves the unchanged product requirements; valid upgrades are accepted and recorded |
| UniTask | Official Git tag `2.5.11` |
| Addressables | Explicit `2.9.1`; Localization's transitive minimum `1.25.0` does not enable our supported backend |
| UGUI / UTF | `2.0.0` / `1.6.0` |
| DOTween | Official `1.3.045` ZIP, fixed URL and SHA-256, with `DOTween.Modules` |
| TMP | Essential Resources bundled with that Editor's UGUI, checked by SHA-256 |

`unity-host.json` records host inputs. UGUI supplies `Unity.TextMeshPro`.
UniTask supplies `UniTask.DOTween`; it is not another download. Standard engine
modules supply physics, animation, particles and the other engine APIs used here.

For this UPM host, `COCOFLOW_UNITASK_SUPPORT` is generated by each assembly's
UniTask `[2.5.11,3.0.0)` versionDefine. Addressables `[2.9.1,3.0.0)` generates
`COCOFLOW_ADDRESSABLES_2_9_OR_NEWER`. Neither is copied as a global manual define.
The active Standalone target explicitly has `COCOFLOW_DOTWEEN_SUPPORT`,
`UNITASK_DOTWEEN_SUPPORT` and DOTween's `DOTWEEN`. Input uses the Input System
backend (`activeInputHandler: 1`).

A host-only EditMode fixture checks the actual Windows Editor/version, required
packages, compiled assemblies, DOTween version and support defines. Product
requirements are not exact-version pins: UPM may resolve a compatible newer
version. The actual versions are recorded in dependencies.json. The result reader requires every
test-bearing CoCoFlow assembly in each mode's XML. Missing UI, Content, Map or
Addressables tests cannot be hidden by compiling those integrations out.
The empty-project build-callback test must execute and pass.

The Utility catalog lists Animation/DOTween and Animation/UniTask adapter
assemblies that do not exist in this package. Catalog entries do not expand CI's
support claim; actual source and asmdefs remain authoritative.

## Personal activation and cleanup

Only `UNITY_EMAIL` and `UNITY_PASSWORD` are required. The working Personal account
does not use `UNITY_LICENSE` or a Student serial.

The Windows job installs the official Editor with its documented silent-install
arguments, validates the release integrity and installer signature, and downloads
the SHA-256-checked GameCI executable. It uses GameCI's official native flow:

    game-ci test .ci-work/host --docker --local --test-platforms "playmode;editmode"

Here `--local` runs the installed Windows Editor directly; no Docker container is
used. No GameCI source is modified. The activation retry limit is one, and test
failures are not retried. Scripts and test changes are verified locally before a
GitHub candidate validation run.

The supported ENGINE_LAUNCH_WRAPPER hook explicitly waits for each Windows GUI
Editor process and forwards its exit code. Without that wait, v0.1.72 can start
PlayMode and EditMode concurrently and attempt license return before they finish;
run 42378865246 demonstrated that race and its licensing-client mutex failure.

Each test Editor process has a ten-minute deadline. The test step has a
twenty-two-minute hard limit, followed in the same Windows job by a separate
three-minute cleanup step using always(). Test case assertions and their own
timeouts are unchanged. This leaves cleanup independent of the test shell's
finally block when the test step fails, times out or is cancelled.

The cleanup step uses this run's explicit ASSIGN_SEAT or Activation complete
evidence, including allocation followed by a command failure. A rejected login
does not start a return command. If GameCI or a previous invocation already
confirmed return, cleanup does not return the seat again.

The pinned native cleanup can stop at its missing-ULF fallback. The separate
cleanup then uses the complete official Personal Editor return arguments,
including -batchmode, and waits up to two minutes. A native successful-return
marker is required; exit zero alone is not a return receipt. license-return.json
records observed activation, fallback use, return confirmation, exit code, log
availability and fixed diagnostic categories without account values. An
unconfirmed return fails the job even when all tests passed. Raw licensing logs
stay outside uploaded artifacts.

The old Personal activation trial workflow has been retired; its history and
prior evidence remain. Routine validation uses the complete Unity workflow.
Cleanup is best effort if the runner disappears or the entire job is forcibly
terminated; such a run must not be reported as a confirmed seat return.

The earlier Linux run also needed a separate return step: its first missing-ULF
attempt did not return the entitlement. The two-attempt cleanup then switched to
the official Editor command and confirmed the return. The Windows flow preserves
one activation attempt and makes one explicit Editor return after that same ULF
fallback condition; it does not increase the activation retry limit.

Unity jobs share one Personal activation concurrency group. An active job keeps
its slot through the bounded cleanup step; pending runs may replace older
pending runs.

## Evidence and failures

The official Unity step must succeed, and both fresh NUnit XML files must be
valid, nonempty, `Passed`, with zero Failed/Inconclusive. Test-bearing assemblies
and dependency/empty-host assertions are required. A result-reader exit zero
cannot override a failed Unity step or failed seat return.

Artifacts contain this run's XML, Editor test logs, dependency evidence, prepared
inputs, manifest/lock and installer/CLI identity. They are named with SHA and run attempt.
License state, authentication logs, full host and Library are not uploaded.
Downloaded evidence can be archived at:

    .ci-artifacts/<SHA>/<host>/<version>/

ScenarioD explicitly creates/registers its runtime persistence identity and
verifies the saved document contains that actor. It does not restore automatic
IDs. Historical 0.4.6 XML stays unchanged. Package discovery/localization
assertions remain; release equality is checked by the release-identity command
instead of a hardcoded C# version.

Windows Editor results do not prove Player, IL2CPP/AOT, stripping, other operating
systems, coverage, performance or visual acceptance. Prior Linux results remain
historical evidence and do not become Windows results. Y releases and task-specific
external checks retain their declared acceptance requirements.

## Release policy

After the new required gate is enabled:

- Z releases keep task acceptance and PRs, then use one closing commit for package
  version, short Changelog, current install references and existing exception
  versions. No separate Release task, version signature or release branch.
- The protected task → `dev/<version>` → master route stays. The closing commit
  can join the last task PR, or use a small PR if tasks already merged.
- Y releases retain a Release task, the declared full Editor/platform/integration
  matrix, migration/contract checks and maintainer version acceptance.
- Z candidates changing public contracts, migration or support boundaries return
  to the maintainer to decide acceptance strength.
- Green CI does not authorize merge, tag, GitHub Release or branch deletion.

Preserve current master/dev PR, thread-resolution, merge-method, bypass and
force-push/delete settings. Only the required check changes from
`CI Static / gate` to `CI / gate`, preserving its GitHub Actions integration.
Do not remove the old requirement before the replacement is proven and deployed.

## Local infrastructure checks

    python3 -m unittest discover -s .github/ci -p 'test_*.py' -v
    python3 .github/ci/cocoflow_ci.py release

These do not prove Unity tests. Persistent 03/05 hosts remain separate;
temporary linkage requires exclusive use and exact manifest/lock restoration.

## Manual Windows Player experiments

The optional workflow_dispatch input `player_probe=true` runs the separate
`Player experiment / Windows Mono` or `Windows IL2CPP` job using the pinned installer,
GameCI CLI, complete host dependencies and Personal-seat cleanup. Ordinary
push/PR/manual runs keep their existing complete Editor path. On this explicit
experiment, the complete Editor job and `CI / gate` are skipped: the probe is
not complete-package release evidence and does not change branch protection.

Select `player_backend=mono` (default, stripping Disabled) or
`player_backend=il2cpp` (stripping Medium). The latter installs the official,
integrity-checked Windows IL2CPP module for the same Unity version and verifies
the runner's Visual C++ x64 compiler and Windows SDK before activation. The
installation receipt records the detected tools and Player variations.

Each probe builds a Windows x64 test Player and
runs six existing binding/config/context/restore cases plus a host-only test
that requires WindowsPlayer, not Editor, with ENABLE_MONO or ENABLE_IL2CPP
matching the requested backend. The reader requires
all seven cases exactly once, consistent counts, no skipped/failed/inconclusive
cases, actual prebuild settings, the executable and confirmed seat return.
A failed GameCI step still fails the job even if result files appear green.
Results certify only the recorded backend, stripping level and selected paths;
they do not certify coverage, other platforms or performance. Test code can
root types that a real game would otherwise strip, so even a passing IL2CPP
probe does not certify arbitrary game builds or High stripping.
Windows Server headless Player startup is an experiment, not an assumed pass.
The build receipt records Unity's native enum name `Mono2x` for Mono. The build
callback compares typed enum values and writes observed settings before a failure.

Example after the experiment branch is explicitly approved and pushed:

    gh workflow run ci-static.yml --ref feat/0.4.8-P001-player-validation -f player_probe=true
    gh workflow run ci-static.yml --ref feat/0.4.8-P001-player-validation -f player_probe=true -f player_backend=il2cpp

Artifacts are named `player-<suite>-<backend>-<SHA>-<attempt>` and include the source SHA,
build settings, executable SHA-256, XML, Player/Editor logs and cleanup receipt.
Account values and the native authentication log are not uploaded.

`player_preserve_metadata=true` is a separate diagnostic experiment. It adds a
host-only link.xml retaining selected module registrar/converter types and
Operation Section metadata, to distinguish stripping failures from subsequent
AOT failures. Prepared inputs and the actual build receipt bind its file hash;
the result summary retains the diagnostic label. Its results cannot certify the
baseline package without those preservation rules. The default remains false;
the rules do not enter the UPM Runtime or a game's build automatically.

For all Player-eligible tests, set `player_suite=all`. The runner omits the name
filter and executes every test compiled into the Player. Editor-only assemblies
and code behind UNITY_EDITOR remain excluded by Unity. Both profiles add one
host-only guard that checks WindowsPlayer and the selected compiled backend.
The full mode rejects diagnostic preservation and retains the original Mono /
Disabled and IL2CPP / Medium profiles. It reports per-assembly totals and every
case's result, failure message, stack or skip reason in player-probe-summary.json.
Missing source-inventoried Runtime test assemblies are reported explicitly;
an absent assembly is not silently counted as tested. Test failures, skips,
missing XML, configuration mismatches and unconfirmed seat return stay red.

    gh workflow run ci-static.yml --ref feat/0.4.8-P001-player-validation -f player_probe=true -f player_suite=all -f player_backend=mono -f player_preserve_metadata=false
    gh workflow run ci-static.yml --ref feat/0.4.8-P001-player-validation -f player_probe=true -f player_suite=all -f player_backend=il2cpp -f player_preserve_metadata=false

The full run allows up to 60 minutes for the build Editor, 85 minutes for the
combined build/test step and 130 minutes for the job, leaving a separate cleanup
step. These are deadlines, not measured duration estimates. Ordinary Editor CI
and the small probe retain their previous deadlines.
